case_metadata.drug_detail: 2.5 mg subcutaneous once weekly, titrated per labeling
case_metadata.policy_pathway: Section 2 — General coverage criteria, A. Initial Authorization
plan_variant_evidence: Denial letter plan line: 'Commercial employer group pharmacy benefit (fully insured, Ohio)'
Denial letter cites Section 2, not Section 3
case_metadata.design_note: The age criterion is drug-dependent within a single subsection: 12 or older for four named products, over 16 for everything else. Zepbound falls in the second group. Everything else about the case is satisfied, so a system that reads the age limb without checking which product it attaches to will overturn a correct denial.

denial_ground_truth.denial_reason_text: The age requirement for Zepbound under this program is greater than 16 years; the patient is 15.

Initial Authorization

scope_notes: The two age limbs are alternatives keyed to the product, not to the patient. Only Qsymia, Saxenda, Wegovy injection and Xenical carry the 12-or-older threshold under Section 2.
The threshold for the second limb is strictly greater than 16, not 16 or older. A 16-year-old would also fail it.

evidence_ground_truth.evidence_timing_note: The 2026-05-04 note was submitted and reviewed. The payer's account of the record is accurate.

expected_evidence.evidence_text: DOB 02/03/2011; age 15 at the time of the request. The note header and the denial both record this.
Not a clinical fact. Recorded because the patient's age of 15 does satisfy the 12-or-older limb, which is the most likely source of an incorrect overturn.
Height 5 ft 8 in, weight 232 lb, BMI 35.3 kg/m2; 236 lb, BMI 35.9, on 02/16/2026.
Assessment item 1 is adolescent obesity; the plan requests tirzepatide for weight.

Nutrition consultation 02/16/2026 with energy drinks stopped and a packed-lunch plan, review 03/23/2026 with football twice weekly and a Saturday club, both maintained. Plan item 1 states the medication is an adjunct to those changes.

missing_evidence.description: No documentation could satisfy the age criterion; it is a matter of date of birth.

per_criterion.reason: The patient is 15. Zepbound is governed by the over-16 limb because it is not one of the four products named in the 12-or-older limb.
Recorded to make the scope explicit: the patient's age would satisfy this limb, but the limb does not reach Zepbound.
The request is for weight loss.
Dietary and activity changes documented from 02/16/2026 and continuing.

supported_claims: Every criterion other than age is satisfied on the submitted record.
The denial accurately quotes the age limb and correctly identifies which limb governs Zepbound.
Lifestyle modification is documented and continuing.
unsupported_claims: That the patient is over 16 years of age.
That the 12-or-older limb applies to Zepbound.
That the patient's BMI or clinical need can displace an age criterion.
appeal_ground_truth.correct_next_step: Advise that the denial cannot be overturned. Worth raising with the prescriber: Wegovy injection is one of the four products the same subsection places under the 12-or-older limb, so a request for that product would clear the age criterion at this patient's age. That is a new request on a different product, not an appeal of this determination.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: The patient's date of birth is February 3, 2011 and he was 15 years of age at the time of the request.
Documented BMI on May 4, 2026 was 35.3 kg/m2, with height 5 feet 8 inches and weight 232 pounds.
A nutrition consultation on February 16, 2026 stopped energy drinks and set a packed-lunch plan.
Football twice weekly and a Saturday club began by March 23, 2026 and have been maintained.
The patient has used no prescription weight-loss medication and has no GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure.
The policy places Qsymia, Saxenda, Wegovy injection and Xenical under a 12-or-older age limb.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The patient is over 16 years of age.
Zepbound is covered under the 12-or-older age limb.
The patient has type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea or another weight-related comorbidity.
The patient has been approved for Zepbound previously.
The patient's BMI is above the 120 percent of the 95th percentile threshold in the North Dakota criteria.
The patient completed a supervised weight management program.
